children: The Indian rupee opened lower against the US dollar at 96.01 on September 17, down 6 paise from the previous close of 95.95, after the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates and signalled further tightening.

According to Finrex, the Indian rupee is expected to open around 96.02 per dollar, with the RBI likely to intervene in the NDF market. The dollar index rose to 100.35 after the US Fed raised rates by 25 bps and signalled another hike at the next meeting, while most Asian currencies weakened against the dollar. Brent crude was slightly lower but remained above its lows.

Finrex expects the RBI to remain active in the market, although the rupee could face near-term pressure amid a stronger dollar, weakness in Asian currencies—particularly the Korean won—and prevailing risk aversion. Exporters are expected to continue selling dollars for up to 12 months, while importers may continue buying on dips for cash and one-week requirements.

Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar in early trade. The Malaysian ringgit declined the most, down 0.57%, followed by the Taiwan dollar (0.30%) and South Korean won (0.25%). The Philippine peso and Thai baht also weakened marginally.
Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah slipped 0.01%, while the Japanese yen gained 0.10%, China’s renminbi rose 0.05% and the Singapore dollar edged up 0.04%.
The dollar held onto Wednesday’s gains after the US central bank raised interest rates and signaled more are coming.
The dollar Spot index stands pat after gaining 0.5% on Wednesday to hit a one-month high. US 10-year yields dropped 2bps to 4.99%.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens 6 paise lower at 96.01 per dollar
